questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with a painless, indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. Inguinal lymphadenopathy is non-tender. Dark field microscopy reveals motile spiral organisms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents as a painless, indurated chancre with non-tender regional lymphadenopathy. Dark field microscopy shows Treponema pallidum. Chancroid is painful; LGV causes tender lymphadenopathy; Donovanosis shows Donovan bodies on biopsy.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer from rural Maharashtra presents with erythematous scaly plaques, alopecia, and onychomycosis. KOH examination of skin scrapings shows septate hyphae with arthroconidia. Which organism is most likely responsible for onychomycosis?
questions.exp: Trichophyton rubrum is the most common cause of tinea corporis, tinea pedis, and onychomycosis worldwide and in India. It shows septate hyphae on KOH and does not fluoresce under Wood's lamp. T. violaceum is more common in scalp infections in India.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with recurrent grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lips, recurring 4-5 times a year. She asks about long-term suppressive therapy. Which antiviral regimen is used for suppression?
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg five times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: For suppressive therapy of recurrent herpes labialis or genitalis, Acyclovir 400 mg twice daily (or Valacyclovir 500 mg once daily) is the standard regimen. Single-dose and short-course regimens are used for episodic treatment, not suppression.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with thickened, nodular earlobes, madarosis, and loss of eyebrows. Slit-skin smear shows a bacterial index of 5+. Which form of leprosy does this represent?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) is characterised by widespread lesions, nodular infiltration of ears, leonine facies, madarosis, loss of eyebrows/eyelashes, and high bacterial index (5-6+). It represents a state of low cell-mediated immunity with high humoral response.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman develops a photosensitive butterfly-shaped rash on the face, oral ulcers, and polyarthralgia. ANA is positive at 1:640 with anti-dsDNA antibodies elevated. Which complement component deficiency is the single strongest genetic risk factor for SLE?
questions.exp: C1q deficiency is the single strongest genetic risk factor for SLE. C1q normally clears apoptotic debris; its deficiency leads to accumulation of nuclear antigens triggering autoimmunity. Anti-dsDNA antibodies are highly specific for SLE and correlate with disease activity.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with tense bullae on normal-appearing skin with pruritus. Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid shows tense bullae on normal or erythematous skin. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. Target antigens are BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230. Pemphigus vulgaris shows intercellular IgG (fish-net pattern) in the epidermis.

questions.q: A 60-year-old smoker presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasia and central ulceration on the nose. The lesion has been slowly growing for 2 years. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer, classically presenting as a pearly nodule with rolled edges, telangiectasia, and central ulceration ('rodent ulcer') on sun-exposed areas of the face. Slow growth over years and absence of metastasis until very late are characteristic.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with silvery-white scales on erythematous plaques on the elbows and knees. The Auspitz sign is positive. Which histological finding is most characteristic of this condition?
questions.exp: Psoriasis histology shows parakeratosis (retained nuclei in stratum corneum), Munro microabscesses (neutrophil collections in stratum corneum), regular acanthosis, suprapapillary plate thinning, and dilated capillaries in dermal papillae. Auspitz sign is punctate bleeding on scale removal.

questions.q: A 25-year-old atopic woman presents with lichenified, pruritic patches in the antecubital and popliteal fossae. Serum IgE is markedly elevated. Which immunological pattern best describes the pathogenesis of her condition?
opts: Th1-dominant response throughout the disease course
Th2-dominant in acute phase shifting to Th1 in chronic phase
CD8+ cytotoxic T cells causing keratinocyte apoptosis
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis has a biphasic immune response: acute lesions are driven by Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-13, IL-31) causing IgE production and eosinophilia; chronic lesions show a shift toward Th1 cytokines (IFN-gamma, IL-12). Dupilumab targets IL-4Ra to block both IL-4 and IL-13.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with ring-shaped lesions on the scalp with broken hair stumps. Wood's lamp examination shows bright green-yellow fluorescence. Culture on Sabouraud's dextrose agar grows a white velvety colony. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis is a zoophilic dermatophyte causing tinea capitis with ectothrix pattern. It produces bright green-yellow fluorescence under Wood's lamp. T. tonsurans and T. violaceum (endothrix) do not fluoresce. M. audouinii is anthropophilic and also fluoresces.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive man presents with multiple pearly, umbilicated papules scattered on the face, neck, and trunk. CD4 count is 80 cells/uL. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (poxvirus) presents as umbilicated pearly papules. In immunocompetent individuals lesions are self-limiting and fewer; in HIV/AIDS with low CD4, lesions are extensive and giant, especially on the face. Cryptococcosis can mimic MC but presents with meningeal symptoms.

questions.q: During a leprosy clinic, a borderline leprosy patient on multidrug therapy suddenly develops painful swelling and redness of existing skin patches, fever, and new nerve tenderness. No new lesions appear. What is this reaction called?
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction is a delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) reaction in borderline leprosy (BT, BB, BL). Existing lesions become inflamed; new lesions do not typically appear. Treated with prednisolone. ENL occurs in BL/LL and features evanescent erythematous nodules with systemic features.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with dysphagia, Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, and calcinosis cutis. Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc), which involves skin proximal to elbows/knees and carries high risk of interstitial lung disease and renal crisis. CREST syndrome (limited SSc) is associated with anti-centromere antibodies.

questions.q: A 19-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on the extensor aspects of elbows and knees with intense pruritus. Biopsy shows subepidermal blisters with neutrophils at dermal papillary tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at the DEJ. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis shows granular (not linear) IgA deposits at the DEJ on DIF. It is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy (celiac disease) and anti-transglutaminase antibodies. Linear IgA disease shows linear IgA deposits and is often drug-induced (vancomycin).

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing nodule on the lower lip that developed over 6 weeks, now 2 cm with a central keratin plug. Biopsy shows well-differentiated squamous cells with a central keratin-filled crater. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing, often self-resolving crateriform lesion with a central keratin plug. Key features: explosive growth over weeks, volcano-shaped architecture on histology. Some authorities consider it a well-differentiated SCC variant, especially on the lip where it rarely regresses.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with violaceous flat-topped papules with Wickham's striae on the flexor wrists and a white lacy pattern on the buccal mucosa. What is the first-line treatment for generalised cutaneous lichen planus?
questions.exp: Oral corticosteroids (prednisolone) are the first-line treatment for generalised or severe lichen planus. Topical steroids are used for localised disease. Oral acitretin is second-line for refractory cases. NB-UVB is an option for widespread disease not responding to systemic steroids.

questions.q: A 42-year-old male from Bihar presents with a progressive, painless skin-coloured to reddish nodular plaque on the nose. Biopsy shows foamy macrophages (Mikulicz cells) containing Gram-negative bacilli. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Rhinoscleroma is caused by Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis, a Gram-negative encapsulated bacillus. Histology shows Mikulicz cells (large vacuolated macrophages with bacilli) and Russell bodies (eosinophilic plasma cells). It causes progressive granulomatous disease of the upper airway.

questions.q: A 26-year-old sexually active woman presents with multiple, soft, painful genital ulcers with undermined edges and tender fluctuant inguinal lymphadenopathy. Gram stain of ulcer exudate shows Gram-negative coccobacilli in a 'school of fish' pattern. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, a Gram-negative coccobacillus. It presents with painful, soft, ragged-edged ulcers and tender suppurative lymphadenopathy (bubo). The 'school of fish' pattern on Gram stain is characteristic. Syphilis is painless; herpes shows multinucleated giant cells.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain reveals Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which is the most appropriate topical therapy for localised impetigo?
questions.exp: Impetigo (non-bullous) caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes is treated with topical mupirocin (first-line) for localised disease. Mupirocin is bactericidal and effective against MRSA. Fusidic acid is an alternative. Systemic antibiotics are reserved for widespread or bullous disease.

questions.q: A 33-year-old woman presents with hypopigmented macules on the trunk that show fine branny scaling when scratched (Zina sign). KOH preparation shows a 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur. KOH shows short hyphae and round spores ('spaghetti and meatballs'). Treatment: selenium sulfide 2.5% or ketoconazole 2% shampoo/lotion topically; oral itraconazole for widespread disease. Terbinafine and griseofulvin have poor activity against Malassezia.

questions.q: A dermatology resident performs a Tzanck smear from the base of a fresh blister. The smear shows multinucleated giant cells. This finding is characteristic of which conditions?
questions.exp: Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells (Tzanck cells) in herpetic infections (HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV). It cannot differentiate between HSV and VZV. Acantholytic cells are seen in pemphigus. PCR or direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) is needed to distinguish HSV from VZV.

questions.q: A 48-year-old man started on dapsone for leprosy develops pallor, jaundice, and dark urine after 2 weeks. Peripheral smear shows Heinz bodies. Which enzyme deficiency predisposes to this complication?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia. G6PD deficiency severely exacerbates haemolysis by impairing the ability of RBCs to neutralise oxidative stress. Heinz bodies are precipitates of denatured haemoglobin. G6PD screening before dapsone initiation is recommended.

questions.q: A 52-year-old woman presents with heliotrope rash around the eyes, Gottron's papules over knuckles, and proximal muscle weakness. Creatine kinase is 3500 U/L. Which malignancy has the strongest association with dermatomyositis in women?
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis is paraneoplastic in approximately 20-30% of adults. In women, ovarian cancer has the strongest association. Other commonly associated cancers include lung, breast, colorectal, and gastric. Thorough malignancy workup is mandatory at diagnosis of dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy presents with recurrent erythema and oedema of the lips, tongue, and face without urticaria, precipitated by minor trauma. C4 level is persistently low and C1 esterase inhibitor level is also low. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Hereditary angioedema type I is an autosomal dominant condition caused by quantitative deficiency of C1-inhibitor. It presents with bradykinin-mediated angioedema without urticaria. C4 is chronically low; C1q is normal. Type II has normal or elevated but dysfunctional C1-INH. Acquired types occur after age 40.

questions.q: A 29-year-old woman has sharply demarcated depigmented patches on the face and hands with complete melanocyte loss confirmed on histology. Wood's lamp shows chalky-white fluorescence. What is the first-line treatment for localised vitiligo on the face?
questions.exp: For localised vitiligo, potent topical corticosteroids (e.g., mometasone, clobetasol) are the standard first-line treatment. Topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) are preferred for the face and sensitive areas to avoid steroid side effects. NB-UVB is preferred for widespread disease.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male with chronic plaque psoriasis refractory to methotrexate is started on adalimumab. Which screening is mandatory before initiating anti-TNF therapy?
opts: Chest X-ray and tuberculin skin test (TST) or IGRA
questions.exp: TNF-alpha inhibitors (adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab) carry high risk of reactivating latent tuberculosis. Guidelines mandate screening with TST (Mantoux) or IGRA (QuantiFERON-TB Gold) plus chest X-ray before initiation. Latent TB must be treated with isoniazid for at least 4 weeks before starting biologics.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a slow-growing, well-defined, flesh-coloured subcutaneous nodule on the upper back present for 20 years. On palpation it feels doughy and mobile. Excision reveals an encapsulated mass of mature adipocytes. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lipoma is a benign tumour of mature adipocytes. It presents as a soft, mobile, encapsulated subcutaneous nodule with a doughy consistency, slow growth, and no skin attachment. Epidermoid cysts have a central punctum and cheesy contents; pilomatricomas are calcified and hard; neurofibromas are associated with NF1.

questions.q: A dermatologist performs patch testing in a 35-year-old woman with suspected contact dermatitis. At 48 and 96 hours the reaction shows erythema, induration, and vesicles. How is this graded according to ICDRG criteria?
questions.exp: ICDRG grading: +/- = doubtful (faint erythema only); + = weak positive (erythema with infiltration); ++ = strong positive (erythema, infiltration, and vesicles); +++ = extreme positive (bullous or ulcerative reaction). Reading at both 48h and 96h is essential to detect late reactions to metals.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman develops fever, odynophagia, and widespread tender erythema followed by epidermal detachment involving 35% of body surface area. Nikolsky sign is positive. She was started on carbamazepine 3 weeks ago. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) is characterised by >30% BSA epidermal detachment, positive Nikolsky sign, mucosal involvement, and systemic toxicity following a drug trigger (carbamazepine is a classic culprit). SSSS occurs mainly in neonates/elderly; blister is subcorneal. SCORTEN score assesses mortality.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male from South India presents with scrotal swelling, multiple discharging sinuses with sulphur granules, and woody induration of the perineum. KOH of granule shows eosinophilic clubs at the periphery ('Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon'). What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Actinomycetoma caused by Actinomadura madurae (a filamentous bacterium, not a true fungus) produces white-pale granules surrounded by Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon (eosinophilic clubs). Eumycetoma (Madurella mycetomatis) shows dark brown-black granules without eosinophilic clubs. Treatment differs significantly.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a dark, irregularly pigmented lesion on the sole of his foot with variegated colour, irregular borders, and diameter of 8 mm. Which histological feature is most critical to report for prognosis?
questions.exp: Breslow's thickness (vertical depth of tumour in mm from granular layer to deepest tumour cell) is the single most important prognostic factor in melanoma. It determines T-staging in the AJCC system and guides sentinel lymph node biopsy decisions (SLNBx recommended if Breslow >0.8 mm with ulceration or >1 mm).
